backlog.title: Bugfix Release v1.0.1 — zoxide flag absorption + single-quote query
backlog.description: Fix two issues found in adversarial QA testing of tmux-zoxide-sessions v1.0: (1) MAJOR — zoxide flag absorption where leading-dash queries (-l/--list) dump the entire frecency database into a corrupted window, caused by a regression that removed the contract-required `--` end-of-options guard; (2) MINOR — single quotes in window-jump queries break resolution due to the binding's single-quoted run-shell argument. Both fixes include defence-in-depth hardening, test fixture improvements, and regression tests.

milestones.title: Issue 1 — zoxide flag absorption fix (Major)
milestones.description: Three-layer fix for the zoxide flag absorption bug: (1) restore the `--` end-of-options guard in _resolve_zoxide, (2) add POSIX-compliant defence-in-depth guards in z-window.sh and z-session.sh that reject multi-line/non-directory resolved values, (3) harden all 6 fake-zoxide test fixtures to model real zoxide's flag parsing and add regression tests for leading-dash queries. The fixture hardening MUST precede the guard restoration because restoring `--` changes the fake zoxide's argv and would break existing tests if fixtures aren't synchronized.

tasks.title: Synchronize resolver `--` guard with hardened test fixtures
tasks.description: Restore the `--` end-of-options guard in _resolve_zoxide (the root fix for Issue 1) while simultaneously hardening all 6 fake-zoxide test fixtures so they remain compatible. The fixture hardening (S1) must be done BEFORE the guard restoration (S2) because restoring `zoxide query -- "$1"` changes the fake zoxide's argv from `query <kw>` to `query -- <kw>`, and every fake must strip `--` or existing proj-match tests silently break.

subtasks.title: Harden all 6 fake-zoxide test fixtures to strip `--` and model list-mode
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/research_issue1_defense.md §D for the exact current state of each fake-zoxide fixture and architecture/findings_and_risks.md §R2 for the list-mode modeling constraint. All 6 fake zoxide binaries share two flaws: (a) a blind `shift` that ignores `--`, and (b) `case "$1"` treating every argument (including `-l`/`--list`) as a plain query returning empty — so real zoxide's list-mode flag parsing is never modeled. There are exactly 6 test files with a fake-zoxide fixture: test_resolve_zoxide.sh, test_resolve_dispatcher.sh, test_z_window.sh, test_z_session.sh, test_run_file.sh, test_backend_matrix.sh (subtest B). Files with NO fake-zoxide (test_resolve_z.sh, test_session_hook.sh) are out of scope.
2. INPUT: No code dependencies. The 6 test files exist at commit 720f1f3 and pass (80/80). The resolver currently calls `zoxide query "$1"` (no `--`), so the fakes' blind `shift` works today.
3. LOGIC: For each of the 6 fake-zoxide fixtures, restructure the argument parsing to model real zoxide's `--` and list-mode behavior:
   - After `shift` (consuming `query`), check if `$1` is `--`. If yes, consume it (shift) and treat everything after as a POSITIONAL argument (literal query) — NEVER enter list mode after `--`.
   - If `--` is NOT present, model real zoxide's flag parsing: for `-l` or `--list`, enter list-mode and print a MULTI-LINE dump (e.g. `printf '%s\n' "/fake/db/entry1" "/fake/db/entry2" "/fake/db/entry3"; exit 0`). This models the bug so regression tests can observe it.
   - For positional queries (after `--` or non-flag), keep the existing `case` match logic (proj/token -> fixture dir, else empty).
   - CRITICAL for test_resolve_dispatcher.sh: its fake exits 1 on no-match (to exercise CORRECTION B's `return 0` in resolve()). Keep that exit-1-on-no-match for the `*` arm. Only the `--` stripping and list-mode (`-l`/`--list`) arms are new; list-mode exits 0 (real zoxide exits 0 in list mode).
   - CRITICAL for test_backend_matrix.sh subtest B: its fake uses an unquoted heredoc (`<<ZOX`) with `$TOKEN`/`$FIX` expansion. Preserve that expansion style.
   - Template for each hardened fake (adapt per-file token/paths):
     ```sh
     #!/bin/sh
     [ "$1" = "query" ] || exit 0
     shift
     if [ "$1" = "--" ]; then
         shift    # -- consumed; everything after is a positional (literal query)
     else
         # No --: model flag parsing (list-mode for -l/--list, like real zoxide)
         case "$1" in
             -l|--list) printf '%s\n' "/fake1" "/fake2"; exit 0 ;;
         esac
     fi
     # Positional query resolution
     case "$1" in
         <token>) printf '%s\n' "<fixture-dir>" ;;   # MATCH
         *)       printf '' ;;                          # no-match -> empty
     esac
     exit 0
     ```
   Also delete/rewrite the false comment in each fake that says `no '--' guard: real zoxide/zoxide-shim do not strip it (would break the shim)` — replace with an accurate comment like `# Strip -- (real zoxide honors end-of-options); model list-mode for -l/--list`.
4. OUTPUT: All 6 fake-zoxide fixtures now (a) strip `--` like real zoxide, (b) model list-mode for `-l`/`--list` when `--` is absent. The existing test suite must STILL PASS 80/80 after this change (because the resolver still calls `zoxide query "$1"` without `--`, so the fakes' `--` stripping is a no-op). This is the prerequisite for P1.M1.T1.S2 (guard restoration).
5. DOCS: none — test fixtures are internal dev artifacts, no user-facing/config/API surface change.

subtasks.title: Restore `--` end-of-options guard in _resolve_zoxide + rewrite false comment
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/system_context.md §4 Layer 1 and architecture/findings_and_risks.md §F1, §F2. The `--` guard was originally added per contract P1.M1.T2.S2/NOTE D, then removed by commit b93e776 on a factually false rationale. Real zoxide enters list mode for `-l`/`--list` without `--` (146+ line dump); with `--`, it treats them as positionals and returns empty.
2. INPUT: P1.M1.T1.S1 has hardened all 6 fake-zoxide fixtures to strip `--`, so they are compatible with the restored guard. The current resolver calls `zoxide query "$1"` (scripts/lib/resolve.sh:19) with a false comment block at lines 12-17.
3. LOGIC: In scripts/lib/resolve.sh, change line 19 from `zoxide query "$1"` to `zoxide query -- "$1"`. Delete the entire false comment block (lines 12-17) and replace with an accurate one-line comment, e.g.:
   ```sh
   # _resolve_zoxide <query> -> single directory from `zoxide query`, or empty.
   # The `--` terminates zoxide options so a leading-dash query (e.g. -l, --list)
   # is treated as a literal search term, not a zoxide flag (list-mode dump).
   _resolve_zoxide() {
       command -v zoxide >/dev/null 2>&1 && zoxide query -- "$1" 2>/dev/null
   }
   ```
   Do NOT add `|| true`, `; return 0`, or `local`. Keep the exact `&&` chain form. The `return 0` at the end of `resolve()` (CORRECTION B) handles any residual exit-status risk.
4. OUTPUT: `_resolve_zoxide` now calls `zoxide query -- "$1"`. The fake-zoxide fixtures (hardened in S1) strip `--` and work correctly. The full test suite must pass (80/80 + any new assertions from S1's list-mode fixture changes — the existing cases are unchanged because `--` stripping is a no-op for the current resolver's non-`--` form... wait, after THIS change the resolver DOES pass `--`. So the fakes will now receive `query -- <kw>`, strip `--`, and match correctly. Verify: `sh tests/test_resolve_zoxide.sh` prints pass=3 fail=0, `sh tests/test_resolve_dispatcher.sh` prints pass=14 fail=0, etc.)
5. DOCS: none — internal resolver implementation detail; README's Backends section says 'zoxide runs `zoxide query <query>`' as a high-level description and the `--` is an implementation detail of safe argument passing, not a user-facing surface change.

tasks.title: Defence-in-depth caller guards (reject multi-line/non-directory resolved values)
tasks.description: Add POSIX-compliant guards to z-window.sh and z-session.sh that reject a resolved value if it contains a newline (multi-line database dump) or is not an existing directory, falling back to the current pane path / no-op. This is belt-and-braces defence so a future resolver regression cannot corrupt a window or pane.

subtasks.title: Add newline-reject + directory-exists guard to z-window.sh
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/research_issue1_defense.md §B and architecture/findings_and_risks.md §F4. The PRD's suggested one-liner uses `$'\n'` (bash-only) and has inverted boolean logic — do NOT copy it. Use the POSIX `case ... in *"$NL"*` idiom with a literal newline variable instead.
2. INPUT: scripts/z-window.sh exists and works for normal queries. The current logic (lines ~27-39):
   ```sh
   query="$*"
   cur=$(tmux display-message -p '#{pane_current_path}' 2>/dev/null)
   [ -z "$cur" ] && cur="$HOME"
   session=$(tmux display-message -p '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null)
   dir="$cur"
   if [ -n "$query" ]; then
       resolved=$(resolve "$query")
       [ -n "$resolved" ] && dir="$resolved"
   fi
   base=$(basename "$dir")
   tmux new-window -t "$session:" -c "$dir" -n "$base"
   ```
3. LOGIC: Add a POSIX newline literal near the top of the script (after sourcing resolve.sh), then replace the resolve/dir-assignment block with a guard that checks: (1) resolved contains no newline (multi-line dump = reject), (2) resolved is an existing directory (`-d`). If either fails, keep dir=$cur.
   ```sh
   # Single newline, POSIX-portable (avoids bash-only $'\n').
   NL='
   '
   ```
   Replace the `if [ -n "$query" ]` block with:
   ```sh
   if [ -n "$query" ]; then
       resolved=$(resolve "$query")
       # Defence in depth: accept `resolved` ONLY if it is a single line that is
       # an existing directory. A multi-line value (e.g. a zoxide list-mode dump)
       # or any non-directory falls back to the current pane path.
       case "$resolved" in
           *"$NL"*) : ;;                  # multi-line -> reject, keep dir=$cur
           *)        [ -d "$resolved" ] && dir="$resolved" ;;
       esac
   fi
   ```
   `base` and `new-window` lines are unchanged — they now always receive a single, existing path.
4. OUTPUT: z-window.sh now rejects multi-line or non-directory resolved values. Normal matches still work (single-line existing directory). Empty/no-match falls back to $cur (unchanged). `sh tests/test_z_window.sh` must pass.
5. DOCS: none — internal hardening, no user-facing behavior change for normal queries.

subtasks.title: Add symmetric defence-in-depth guard to z-session.sh
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/research_issue1_defense.md §C. The z-session.sh attack surface is lower (session names rarely contain leading dashes), but the guard belongs for symmetry and future-proofing — the resolver is shared and backend-pluggable.
2. INPUT: scripts/z-session.sh exists with the resolve/respawn sequence (lines ~49-55):
   ```sh
   resolved=$(resolve "$name") || exit 0
   [ -n "$resolved" ] || exit 0
   tmux respawn-pane -t "$pane" -c "$resolved" -k 2>/dev/null || exit 0
   ```
3. LOGIC: Add the same POSIX newline literal (`NL='\n'` with a real newline) near the top, then insert a guard between the `[ -n "$resolved" ]` check and `respawn-pane`:
   ```sh
   # Defence in depth: accept `resolved` ONLY if it is a single existing
   # directory; otherwise no-op (pane stays where it is).
   case "$resolved" in
       *"$NL"*) exit 0 ;;                 # multi-line dump -> refuse to relocate
       *)       [ -d "$resolved" ] || exit 0 ;;
   esac
   ```
   On failure the handler `exit 0`s (consistent with its existing no-op contract) rather than corrupting the pane.
4. OUTPUT: z-session.sh now rejects multi-line or non-directory resolved values. Normal relocations still work. `sh tests/test_z_session.sh` must pass.
5. DOCS: none — internal hardening.

milestones.title: Issue 2 — single-quote query breakage fix (Minor)
milestones.description: Fix the binding quoting so that a window-jump query containing a single quote (e.g. a directory like o'brien) is delivered intact to z-window.sh. The root cause is that the `%%` substitution in the command-prompt binding is raw text with no escaping, and wrapping it in single quotes causes a typed `'` to terminate the argument prematurely. The fix wraps `%%` in shell double quotes within the existing single-quoted run-shell argument.

tasks.title: Fix binding quoting for arbitrary characters and add regression test
tasks.description: Change the run-shell binding in tmux-zoxide-sessions.tmux to wrap `%%` in double quotes so single quotes (and spaces) survive both tmux's lexer and sh -c. Update the test_run_file.sh assertion that checks the binding format. Add an integration regression test proving a single-quote query resolves correctly.

subtasks.title: Double-quote `%%` in the run-shell binding + update test_run_file.sh C3 assertion
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See architecture/research_issue2_quoting.md. tmux `%%` is a raw textual substitution with no escaping. The binding currently wraps `%%` in single quotes: `"run-shell '$CURRENT_DIR/scripts/z-window.sh %%'"`. When a user types a query with `'` (e.g. `o'brien`), the apostrophe terminates the single-quoted run-shell argument prematurely. The fix wraps `%%` in double quotes: `"run-shell '$CURRENT_DIR/scripts/z-window.sh \"%%\"'"` (in the bash run file, `\"` produces a literal `"` in the emitted tmux template, so tmux sees `run-shell '.../z-window.sh "%%"'`). tmux's outer single quotes pass the inner `"..."` through untouched; sh -c then protects `'` and spaces inside double quotes. Trace for `o'brien`: substitute -> `run-shell '.../z-window.sh "o'brien"'` -> tmux lex -> shell cmd `.../z-window.sh "o'brien"` -> sh -c -> $1=o'brien. For empty query (Enter): `""` -> empty $1 -> matches existing fallback behavior.
2. INPUT: tmux-zoxide-sessions.tmux line ~18 currently has: `"run-shell '$CURRENT_DIR/scripts/z-window.sh %%'"`. test_run_file.sh has assertion C3: `contains "C3: abs path to z-window.sh + %% kept" "$b" "run-shell '$REPO_ROOT/scripts/z-window.sh %%'"`.
3. LOGIC: In tmux-zoxide-sessions.tmux, change the binding from `"run-shell '$CURRENT_DIR/scripts/z-window.sh %%'"` to `"run-shell '$CURRENT_DIR/scripts/z-window.sh \"%%\"'"`. In test_run_file.sh, update C3's needle from `"run-shell '$REPO_ROOT/scripts/z-window.sh %%'"` to `"run-shell '$REPO_ROOT/scripts/z-window.sh \"%%\"'"` (or a substring that matches the new form). Verify with `sh tests/test_run_file.sh` that the binding registration test passes.
4. OUTPUT: The registered tmux binding now wraps `%%` in double quotes. test_run_file.sh passes with updated assertion. The existing test suite must remain green (this change only affects the binding format string, not resolver/handler logic).
5. DOCS: none — the README's 'Window jump' usage section does not document the exact quoting of the binding. No user-facing/config surface change (the key, prompt, and behavior are identical for normal queries).
